blocks.body:
## Technical summary

**Best result: 88.45% validation macro F1.** The frozen OaF-style plus spectral ensemble improves the protected 85.05% baseline by 3.40 percentage points, but remains 1.55 points below the requested 90% target. It is therefore not approved for a 90% claim or paid launch.

This result covers 120 untouched Groove validation recordings and 12 naturally supported exact drum classes at a two-frame onset tolerance. No fresh sealed test set exists, and the previously opened Groove test split was not reused.

## Frequency-aware modeling closed most—but not all—of the gap

The single frequency-aware checkpoint reached 86.67%. Freezing a per-class decoder across that model and the prior spectral checkpoint raised the same validation cohort to 88.45%. The bars compare only like-for-like full-validation results; the 90% line is a target, not a measured model.

## Three cymbal articulations now dominate the remaining error

Pedal hi-hat (73.38%), ride (78.55%), and open hi-hat (80.63%) are the weakest supported classes. Kick, cross-stick, high tom, mid tom, and floor tom all exceed 95%. Closing the aggregate gap requires better natural articulation data rather than another aggregate threshold sweep.

## Scope and metric definition

Macro F1 is the unweighted mean of exact-class onset F1 across the 12 classes with natural Groove labels. Each class pools true positives, false positives, and false negatives across all 120 validation recordings, using a ±2-frame match tolerance. Low tom and tambourine have no natural support and are excluded from the supported-class metric; counting both as zero yields 75.81% strict 14-class macro F1.

## Model and validation design

The primary model is a clean-room frequency-aware 2D CNN, projection layer, and bidirectional LSTM trained on the licensed DrumScribe corpus. The secondary model is the protected spectral-MoE checkpoint. Per-class convex, maximum, or noisy-OR probability rules, thresholds, and peak distances were selected on validation and frozen in a config that pins both checkpoint SHA-256 hashes. The new evaluator rejects hash mismatches and never recalibrates on the requested evaluation split.

## Limitations and robustness checks

**No generalization claim is available yet.** The only prior Groove test set has already been opened and cannot be reused for tuning or confirmation. This benchmark measures isolated-drum onset classification, not full-mix separation, beat alignment, notation assignment, export, or browser completion. Low tom and tambourine also lack natural validation support.

A low-rate E-GMD continuation regressed to 86.36% and was rejected. YourMT3 and ADTOF research diagnostics were materially weaker on the evaluated slices; ADTOF is additionally excluded from production by its non-commercial model terms.

## Recommended next steps

1. Freeze this 88.45% ensemble as the comparison baseline.
2. Collect or license natural pedal/open hi-hat and ride-articulation recordings for development.
3. Train the frequency-aware model on that material without touching a future test set.
4. Create a new rights-cleared sealed test set before the next experiment begins.
5. Require more than 90% on development validation, one-time confirmation on the new sealed set, and the complete full-mix product gates before selling an accuracy claim.

## Further questions

- How much natural articulation data is required to lift pedal hi-hat and ride above 85% without harming snare and crash?
- Does the ensemble retain its gain after drum isolation from commercial full mixes?
- Can the new sealed set supply at least 100 natural events for every canonical class, including low tom and tambourine?
